---
status: accepted, partially superseded by ADR 0016
---

# A Render is generated by its own provider, asynchronously, from the PM's words only

A Render is a concept picture of what a Project delivers (CONTEXT.md).
The PM types a description, the app generates an image, and everyone building the thing argues with one picture instead of one paragraph each.
Three decisions in that sentence were not obvious.

## The image provider is not the Assistant's model

The Assistant runs on a model the User configures with their own `OPENAI_API_KEY` (ADR 0007).
Renders run on `POLLINATIONS_API_KEY`, a separate provider behind `src/server/modules/renders/provider.ts`, and the two never meet.

The reason is who pays.
The render preview is offered as a free part of the app, so it must not quietly spend the key a User configured for their own Assistant.
Sharing one provider would also couple two very different failure modes: an Assistant that cannot answer is a degraded conversation, while an image service that is rate limited is one card on one tab.
Each degrades on its own now, and each says so in its own words.

The cost is a second key, a second thing to configure and a hand-rolled client rather than the AI SDK, which does not model this provider's image endpoint.
That is accepted: the client is one `fetch`, and `getModel()`'s null-object pattern is copied exactly, so the app boots with neither key and each surface explains itself.

## Only what the PM typed is sent

Superseded by ADR 0016: the PM may draft the description from up to three pieces of Evidence, and the rule is now that only what the PM approved is sent.
The reasoning below still explains why nothing else is ever added to the prompt.

The prompt is the PM's own sentence. Project data - name, key, Tasks, Evidence - is never mixed into it, and a test asserts that.

A prompt leaves our server for a third party, so what leaves should be only what was written for that purpose.
Building a "better" prompt out of the Project description would send customer data to a free external service as a side effect of clicking a button, which is not a trade the PM was offered.
It also makes the feature explainable: the card shows the sentence, the model and the seed, and those three reproduce the image.

`safe=privacy,secrets` is set on every call as a backstop, not as the control.
The control is that no Project data is in the prompt.

## The request and the picture are separate

`rendersService.request` records a pending Render and returns.
`fulfil` does the slow work in `after()`, and the open tab polls `renderStatesAction` until the row settles, exactly as the message pane waits for Chat Messages (ADR 0011).

Generation takes between five and ninety seconds, which no server action should hold open.
The row is therefore the PM's receipt: it exists, it is theirs, and it will resolve.
A provider failure is written to that row as `state: failed` with a message meant for a human, rather than thrown, because a failure the PM can read is worth more than a spinner that never stops.
`settleIfPending` makes the settle conditional, so a slow generation cannot overwrite a Render the PM deleted and re-created while it was running.

Reusing ADR 0011's polling rather than adding SSE or a job queue keeps the count of moving parts flat; the poll stops as soon as nothing is pending.

## Renders are their own table, not Evidence

Evidence is what the PM uploads as the truth of what happened.
A Render is something the app made up on request.
Storing generated pictures among uploaded artifacts would blur exactly the distinction that makes Evidence worth trusting, so `renders` is its own table with its own tab, and reuses only the `getStorage()` seam for bytes.

## Consequences

- A Render records an Activity Event like any other Project item (ADR 0005); `render` is a new `EntityType`, so `entity_type` needed an enum migration.
- The provenance shown on a card is real: prompt, model and seed reproduce the image, including for the seeded samples, which carry the seeds they were actually generated with.
- There is a hard cap of `RENDER_MAX_PER_PROJECT` renders per Project, checked inside the transaction so two fast clicks cannot both pass it.
- The seed imports committed images through `rendersService.importReady`, so `npm run db:seed` stays offline and a fresh clone shows the tab working with no API key.
- Nothing here forecasts anything. A Render says what the thing should look like, not whether it will be delivered. Risk lives in Risk.
